title: Full Adder: Three Bits In, Two Bits Out
topic: A full adder takes A, B, and a carry-in bit and produces a sum bit and a carry-out bit. Internally it's two XORs, two ANDs and one OR — Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin, Cout = (A·B) + Cin·(A ⊕ B). The genuine motion cycles through all eight input combinations: highlighted truth-table rows, live wire colors, and updated output bits.

beats.narration: Adding two bits is easy. Adding three bits in one box — that's the full adder.

elements.content: Three bits in. Two bits out.

beats.narration: Three inputs — A, B, and a carry from the column on the right. Eight combinations. Each row produces a sum bit and a carry out bit.

elements.content: Three-column input header A, B, Cin and two-column output Sum, Cout
the sum bit toggles often, the carry only when at least two inputs are 1

beats.narration: Build it from gates. Sum equals A xor B xor C in. Carry out is one whenever at least two inputs are one — two ANDs and an OR cover that.

elements.content: XOR chain: (A xor B) feeds the second XOR with Cin → Sum
AND of A·B, AND of (A xor B)·Cin, OR feeding Cout
Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin   ·   Cout = AB + Cin(A ⊕ B)

beats.narration: Step through all eight combinations and watch the wires light up. The sum and carry update with no extra logic — that's a single adder cell working.

beats.narration: Chain n of these and you've got an n-bit ripple-carry adder — the simplest way to add binary numbers in hardware.
